correctness.rationale: PASS: For any q-letter permutation P and k copies, greedily matching a root V uses exactly 1+d(V) periods, with weak descents when consecutive letters are not increasing. Matching VV requires exactly 1+2d(V)+b(V), where b is the closing weak descent; this proves iff criterion. Trace of q-by-q matrix M(u), with lower triangle weight u and upper 1, evaluates by rank-one determinant and geometric series to F=zt^2[sum_(j=0)^(q-1) B^j + q t B^(q-1)]/(1-t^2 B^q), B=1+(1-t^2)z. Every symbol appears k times, giving upper half-length q floor(k/2); cyclic strictly increasing run equality forces one longest root for even k and q rotated longest roots for odd k>=3. Independently enumerated all distinct subsequences for eleven small (q,k) profiles including q=3,k=4 values 3,9,17,15,6,1 and checked maximal roots; finite tests only supplement the general proof.
residual_risks: Host is a complete fixed permutation period repeated k times; no arbitrary repeated-letter period.
